raw.raw:
The hand extends. Thirty feet compressed into nothing. Spectral fingers touch the man's shoulder.

He moves.

Slow. Painful. Like something remembering how joints work.

Not dead.

[CONDITION_REMOVED:Bloodied Nose]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]

His head comes up. Eyes open. Wrong colour. The irises have gone the same greenish-white as the cave light. Not blind. Something worse than blind. Seeing too much, maybe. Or seeing something else entirely.

His mouth moves. No sound.

Then sound. Cracked. Unused.

"Is it time?"

You don't answer that yet. You look at him properly. Two years down here. Coat rotted to the shoulders. Skin the colour of old tallow. Thin in the way that suggests he stopped needing food somewhere along the process rather than ran out of it.

The terminus stone at his back pulses once. Faint. Greenish.

He's been sitting against it for a very long time.

Frizwick makes a quiet sound behind you. Not fear. Recognition of something terrible.

The man's eyes find you. Through you, almost.

"The mechanism," he says. Slow. "Is it time?"

[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[XP:300]
[QUEST_STEP:Assault on Thistletop|Neutralise the threat below the waterline|false]

Already done.

The hand is still there. Still touching his shoulder. He already woke up. Already spoke.

He's looking at you now. Through you. Those green-white eyes patient in a way that costs something to look at. He asked his question and he's waiting. He's been waiting two years. Another few seconds is nothing to him.

Frizwick shifts her weight. Doesn't speak.

The terminus stone pulses again. Slow. Regular. Like breathing.

You need to answer the man.

You turn. Look up the staircase. One hand. Two fingers. Come down.

A pause.

Then footsteps. Careful ones. Morwen descends with her hand on the wall, reading the stone as she goes. She reaches the bottom, takes in the cave, takes in the terminus stone, takes in the man against it.

Her face does the thing it does. Cataloguing. Filing.

She crosses to him. Crouches. Not close enough to touch. Close enough to look.

She looks at his eyes first. Then his hands. Then the stone at his back. Her own hand drifts to her disc amulet without her noticing.

"How long have you been touching it?" she asks.

The man considers this. Like the question requires translation.

"Since the second winter," he says.

Morwen glances back at you. Her expression is controlled and that means it's bad.

She looks at the stone again. The spiral rune carved into its face. The same geometry as her disc. As yours.

"He's sustained," she says quietly. "Not fed. Sustained. There's a difference."

The man nods. Like he knew that. Like he's been knowing it alone down here for a very long time.

"The mechanism," he says again. "Is it time?"

"Yes," you say. "It's time."

Something moves across his face. Not relief. Older than relief. The expression a man makes when he stops holding something very heavy and his arms don't know what to do.

He puts both hands flat on the stone.

"Then I need to stand," he says. "Help me stand."

Morwen looks at you. The question is plain. Touching him means touching something the terminus stone has been running through for two years. She doesn't know what that does to a person. She doesn't know what touching that person does to you.

Neither do you.

Frizwick is already moving. Practical as always. She gets a hand under his arm before either of you decides anything.

He's lighter than he looks. Much lighter.

He gets upright. Sways. Those green-white eyes find the staircase.

"I need to be at the junction stone," he says. "When it happens."

Then he looks at you directly. Really looks. First time.

"You're the outside party," he says. It isn't a question. "Informed. Willing."

A pause.

"The contract requires it," he says. "Someone has to strike the stone who isn't bound to it. That's you."

He already knew. He's been waiting for you specifically.

"Morwen." You keep your voice low. "Sustained. What does that mean for him?"

She doesn't answer immediately. She's still looking at where his hands were pressed against the stone. Two pale prints, already fading.

"The mechanism runs on accumulated resonance," she says. "Greed. Desperation. Ten thousand years of it stored under pressure." She pauses. "The terminus stone is the discharge point. Whatever passes through it on the way to the sea."

She looks at Aldus. He's watching her explain him like it's a weather report about somewhere he used to live.

"He's been sitting in the outflow," she says. "Not enough to kill him. Enough to keep him from dying."

"Enough to change him," you say.

"Yes."

You look at Aldus. The green-white eyes. The wrong-coloured light behind them.

"Is it reversible?"

Morwen is quiet for a moment too long.

"I don't know," she says. "Once the stone discharges fully and the mechanism dissolves." She stops. "The thing sustaining him stops too."

Aldus has been listening to all of this without expression.

"I know," he says. Flat. Calm. "I knew before the first winter."

He chose to stay anyway. Two years against a stone that was slowly making him into something else.

That's either very brave or very broken.

Probably both.

You get his other arm. Between you and Frizwick, you take the stairs.

He's cooperative. Weightless in the wrong way. Like something essential has been redistributed.

The stairs are steep and he manages them without complaint. One step. Another. His feet remember how this works even if the rest of him is somewhere else.

The green light fades behind you. The blue-white channels pick up. The hum returns. Louder here. Closer to threshold.

The junction chamber opens up.

The creature is where you left it. Watching. Those almost-human eyes track Aldus the moment he appears. Something shifts in its posture. Recognition, maybe. Or the contractual equivalent.

Daeris is against the wall. She looks up. Takes in Aldus. Her hand tightens around the river stone.

You bring him to the junction stone. Set him in front of it.

He looks at the script. Runs one hand across the surface without touching it. Reading it the way a man reads a gravestone with his own name on it.

"Four channels first," he says. "In sequence. Then the strike."

The creature moves to the nearest channel. Waiting. Ready to show you the order.

Aldus straightens. As much as he can.

"I'd like to know your name," he says. "Before it happens."

[QUEST_STEP:Assault on Thistletop|Sever the four intake channels in sequence|false]

Already done.

You're here. All of you. The junction chamber. The hum in the walls. The four channels running blue-white and too fast.

Aldus is standing at the stone. The creature is waiting by the first channel. Daeris is against the wall with her river stone. Morwen is reading the room. Frizwick has her hand near her blade from habit.

Aldus asked your name.

You look at the creature. Gesture at the nearest channel. Then the next. A question with your hands.

Show me the order.

It moves. No hesitation. Ten thousand years of knowing exactly what to do and finally someone asking.

It goes to the northeast channel first. Touches the housing. The script around the fitting glows briefly, brighter than the ambient light. Then it steps to the southeast. Northwest. Southwest. Each one in turn, deliberate, the way you'd show a child how to count.

Northeast. Southeast. Northwest. Southwest.

Then it steps back. Looks at you.

Waiting.

Frizwick is already unslinging the charges. Four of them. She lines them up on the stone floor without being asked. Professional. Efficient. She looks at you for placement confirmation.

Morwen is watching the channel flow rates. Her hand is on her disc.

"The fluid will back up between each severance," she says. "Pressure in the remaining lines increases. The last cut will be the hardest."

Aldus hasn't moved from the junction stone. Those green-white eyes on you.

He still wants your name.

The creature wants to finish what it started ten thousand years ago.

The mechanism wants to wake up.

Pick your order.

"Ammut."

He repeats it. Quietly. Like he's filing it somewhere permanent.

"Ammut." A pause. "Good name."

He turns back to the junction stone. Both hands at his sides. Not touching it yet. Waiting for the sequence to complete before whatever happens to him happens.

Daeris makes a small sound. Not words. Just acknowledgment of something.

You look at her. She's looking at Aldus with an expression you haven't seen on her before. Not professional. Not calculating. Something older and considerably less defended.

"He knew," she says. Quiet. To no one in particular. "He knew what it would do and he stayed."

Nobody answers that.

The creature stands by the northeast channel. Patient. Eternal. Ready.

Frizwick holds the first charge. Looks at you.

The hum in the walls pitches slightly higher. The fluid moves faster than it did ten minutes ago.

Running out of time to be careful about this.

Frizwick hands it over. You take it.

The northeast channel housing is warm. The script around the fitting pulses in time with the hum. You press the charge against the joint where the feed line meets the stone. The blasting charge adheres. Frizwick passes you the striker cord without being asked.

You step back.

Look at the creature.

It nods. One slow, deliberate movement.

You pull the cord.

The crack is sharp and small in the enclosed space. Everyone flinches except Aldus. The housing splits clean. Blue-white fluid sprays and then stops. The channel goes dark at the northeast point.

The hum changes pitch. The other three lines brighten immediately. Morwen was right. Pressure redistributing.

The creature moves to the southeast channel without being asked.

Frizwick is already holding the second charge.

[QUEST_STEP:Assault on Thistletop|Sever the four intake channels in sequence|false]

Something drips from the broken housing. Hits the floor. The stone where it lands goes briefly, brilliantly white. Then dark.

Daeris pulls her feet back from it without comment.

Three channels left. The lines are running visibly faster now. The junction stone at the centre of the room is starting to warm. You can feel it from four feet away.
